source_review.notes: Retrieved and reviewed all ten destinations: PostgreSQL 18 EXPLAIN, planner, index-order, collation, and REL_18_STABLE merge/sort executor sources; Graefe's survey; CMU Fall 2023 join notes; and current SQLite and DuckDB ordering documentation. Verified current merge-plan/sort evidence, B-tree direction and NULL ordering, collation scope/version concerns, PostgreSQL mark/restore and fill states, and engine-specific order defaults. Product, source-code, research, and teaching claims are separately scoped.

evidence: Checked L, R, join equality, comparator, equality bands, page/buffer/run notation, residuals, match flags, mark/restore, and delivered order.
Checked sorting equivalence, SQL TRUE equality, comparator-zero candidate alignment, and presentation order remain distinct.
Checked logarithm/fan-in and total cost expressions define assumptions and ceiling terms.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The module does not treat ordering as a boolean or comparator zero as final join truth.

evidence: Independently reproduced five inner, seven left, and nine full rows; semi A/A2/C; anti B/N; and four leading key comparisons.
Recomputed the two-by-three duplicate product as six occurrences.
Recomputed 80 and 20 initial runs, 320,000 and 80,000 sort I/Os, plus 100,000 materialized join reads for 500,000 modeled transfers.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Independent evidence is retained in artifacts/reviews/DBE-055/independent-recomputation.txt; I/O totals are explanatory page models.

evidence: Reviewed monotonic progress: a smaller current key cannot match the other stream's current or future keys.
Reviewed maximal equal-band Cartesian product followed by equality/residual qualification and per-occurrence join-kind state.
Reviewed composition of bag-preserving compatible sorts with merge correctness and exact delivered-key order.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Cost and order conclusions are conditional on comparator compatibility and verified sorted inputs.

evidence: Reviewed empty/exhausted sides, duplicates, NULL/null-safe variants, residual partial matches, composite/mixed direction keys, ties, and all join kinds.
Reviewed one/huge bands, in-memory/multi-pass/incremental sorts, index versus explicit order, wide rows, heavy output, and concurrent spills.
Reviewed collation/provider version changes, NaNs/encoding/time zones, comparator errors, disorder, corrupt/disk-full spill, cancellation, retry, worker-local versus global order, and cleanup.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Comparator/version uncertainty, disorder, or spill corruption requires safe failure/rebuild/fallback rather than silent merge progress.

evidence: Checked both streams share exact type/coercion/collation/direction/NULL semantics and equal keys form contiguous bands.
Checked every occurrence survives, residuals control matches, mark/restore replays exact bands, and unmatched output occurs once after proof of absence.
Checked memory/file ownership, cancellation, ordering identity, and stable-tie disclaimers.
invariant_checking.notes: A later unordered operator invalidates the merge's delivered order unless another enforcer restores it.

evidence: Reviewed the consumed-prefix invariant and safe smaller-key advancement.
Reviewed equal-band maximality, cross-product completeness, residual soundness, and outer/semi/anti match transitions.
Reviewed sort-permutation plus merge composition and the separate proof for output order.
proof_review.notes: Temporal/range joins are identified as separate algorithms with additional active-set proofs.

evidence: The executable is labeled finite and excludes SQL comparator complexity, MVCC, sorting/spill, faults, and performance.
External-sort formulas explicitly state simplified run/fan-in assumptions and implementation omissions.
Current engine order behavior and durable algorithm claims are attributed by version and role.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Observed tie order and finite comparisons are not presented as universal stability or performance proof.

evidence: Repository verification passed one standard-library Python snippet with exact eight-line stdout, empty stderr, zero exit status, and recorded toolchain.
Independent recomputation reproduced bags, comparisons, duplicate output, runs, and I/O arithmetic.
All ten reference artifacts were retained under artifacts/references/DBE-055 and all local links resolved.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live DBMS merge join, external sort, spill/fault schedule, collation upgrade, parallel execution, or production benchmark was run.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed comparator/equality foundations, monotonic merge, duplicate bands, residual-aware join kinds, sort composition, existing/delivered order, memory/skew, comparator correctness, diagnosis, and verification as one coherent single-node treatment.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed evidence for input properties, estimates/actuals, sort methods/runs/memory/temp, bands/fanout, collations, indexes, workers, first/last-row latency, concurrency, cleanup, and remedies spanning statistics, projection, order, indexes, memory, and algorithm choice.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter derives the merge invariant, makes duplicate groups central, provides executable inner/left/full/semi/anti evidence, twelve misconceptions, ten varied examples, and five exercises progressing to temporal-join transfer with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary-source, source-code, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, PostgreSQL/SQLite/DuckDB or executor/optimizer maintainer, collation expert, performance, reliability, operations, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither universal comparator/equality compatibility, correctness of any named implementation, safe external sorting under every failure, stable tie order, estimator or I/O-model accuracy, actual memory/temp/parallel performance, correctness of temporal/range variants, workload-independent algorithm choice, certification, nor deployment fitness.
